parameters.content:
## Automatic SEO Site Architecture Generator

Feed it a large keyword list - up to 10,000 - and it comes back with a Pillar → Cluster → Supporting-page site architecture. Because a keyword list that size can't go into one AI call, the first pass is purely algorithmic: keywords are grouped into raw clusters by shared core terms (stopwords and modifiers like "best"/"free"/"2026" stripped out first). Those clusters are then sent to Claude in batches to get a human-readable topic label and a suggested parent pillar for each - since different batches can independently invent slightly different names for the same pillar, a consolidation pass merges near-duplicate pillar labels into one clean set. The clusters are then assembled under their canonical pillars, and a final review agent checks the resulting architecture for balance and proposes an internal-linking plan.

### How to set up
1. Import this workflow into n8n
2. Add credentials: Anthropic, your CMS/content-planning API (optional, for pushing the finished architecture somewhere), and WhatsApp Business Cloud
3. Edit Set - Config: batchSize (clusters per AI labeling call), maxSampleKeywordsPerClusterForPrompt, the CMS save endpoint, the Anthropic model, and your WhatsApp sender + recipient
4. POST {keywords: [...]} (or {csvText: "..."}) to Webhook - Ingest Keyword List with your full keyword export
5. Use the Manual Trigger to test end to end with a small bundled sample list

### How to customize
- Swap the term-overlap clustering in Code 2 for embedding-based similarity if you want semantically related keywords with no shared words (e.g. "CRM" and "customer relationship management") to land in the same raw cluster
- Have Code 3 pull in real search volume/CPC data before picking each cluster's primary keyword, instead of falling back to phrase length
- Feed API 3's thinPillars/broadPillars flags back into another consolidation pass automatically rather than just reporting them
- Lower batchSize if clusters have very long sample keyword lists and you're hitting token limits

## 1. Keywords (10,000 in)

- **Webhook - Ingest Keyword List**: receives {keywords: [...]} (strings or {keyword, searchVolume, cpc} objects) or {csvText: "..."} to kick off a run.
- **Manual Trigger - Test Run**: runs the workflow by hand for testing.
- **Code 1 - Ingest & Normalize Keywords**: reads whichever payload came in, trims and de-duplicates (case-insensitive), caps the list at maxKeywords, and falls back to a small bundled sample spanning a few topics when the payload is empty so manual runs are testable end to end.
- **Set - Config**: defines batchSize, maxSampleKeywordsPerClusterForPrompt, maxKeywords, the CMS save endpoint, the Anthropic model, and the WhatsApp sender + recipient.

## 2. Coarse Clustering (algorithmic, no AI)

- **Code 2 - Coarse Cluster Keywords By Term Overlap**: strips stopwords and common modifiers (best, free, 2026, etc.) from each keyword, then groups keywords that share the exact same remaining core terms into a raw cluster - this is what turns 10,000 individual keywords into a much smaller, AI-sized number of clusters, with no API calls at all.
- **Code 3 - Compute Primary & Supporting Keywords Per Cluster**: within each raw cluster, picks the keyword with the highest search volume (or, lacking that, the shortest phrasing) as the cluster's hub-page keyword, and marks the rest as supporting-page keyword candidates.
- **Code 4 - Build Cluster Batch Queue**: splits the full cluster list into batches of batchSize for the AI labeling loop that follows.

## 3. Cluster Labeling (AI, batched)

- **Code 5 - Get Next Cluster Batch From Queue**: pops one batch of clusters off the queue each cycle - the loop-back point for every subsequent batch.
- **IF - Cluster Batch Queue Empty**: true when every batch has been labeled, moving on to pillar consolidation; false continues to the next batch.
- **API 1 - Assign Cluster Topics & Pillars (Claude)**: for each cluster in the batch, generates a short human-readable clusterTopic and a broader suggestedPillar it should live under.
- **Code 6 - Parse & Accumulate Batch Results**: parses that response (with a safe per-cluster fallback if a signature is missing from the reply), attaches the labels back onto the matching clusters by signature, appends them to the running labeledClusters list, and loops back to Code 5.

- **Code 7 - Aggregate Distinct Suggested Pillars**: since clusters were labeled in isolated batches, the same underlying pillar can end up with several slightly different names - this counts every distinct raw pillar label with how many clusters used it and a sample of their topics.
- **API 2 - Consolidate Pillar Labels (Claude)**: merges those raw labels into the smallest clear, non-overlapping set of canonical pillar topics.
- **Code 8 - Parse Pillar Consolidation & Build Pillar Mapping**: parses that response into a rawLabel → canonicalPillar lookup, with any label the AI didn't place falling back to becoming its own pillar.

## 5. Assemble Architecture & Review

- **Code 9 - Assemble Final Site Architecture**: applies the pillar mapping to every labeled cluster, groups them under their canonical pillar, generates URL-friendly slugs at every level, and builds the pillar → cluster → supporting-page tree with summary counts.
- **API 3 - Architecture Review Agent (Claude)**: reviews the pillar list for balance, flags pillars that look too thin (should be merged) or too broad (should be split), recommends a hub-and-spoke internal-linking pattern, and suggests which pillars to build out first.
- **Code 10 - Parse Architecture Review & Build Final Report**: parses that response and assembles the final report: summary stats, the full pillar/cluster/supporting-page tree, and the architecture review.

## 6. Output

- **HTTP Request - Save Site Architecture To CMS/Database**: (optional) pushes the finished architecture to a CMS or content-planning system.
- **WhatsApp - Send Completion Summary**: sends the headline numbers - pillars, clusters, supporting pages - and the suggested build priority.
- **Respond to Webhook - Return Site Architecture**: returns the full final report as the webhook's JSON response (a harmless no-op on manual-trigger test runs, which have no webhook to respond to).

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ model: $json.anthropicModel, max_tokens: 4000, system: 'You are an SEO information architect. You are given a batch of keyword clusters, each already grouped algorithmically by shared core terms. For each cluster, give it a short, human-readable topic label (clusterTopic) and the broader pillar topic it should live under (suggestedPillar) - the pillar should be a general content category, not a repeat of the cluster\'s own specific topic. Respond ONLY with valid JSON, no prose, matching exactly this shape: {\"clusters\": [{\"signature\": string, \"clusterTopic\": string, \"suggestedPillar\": string}]}. Return exactly one entry per cluster given, using its signature unchanged so it can be matched back.', messages: [ { role: 'user', content: JSON.stringify(($json.currentBatch || []).map(c => ({ signature: c.signature, keywordCount: c.keywordCount, sampleKeywords: c.sampleKeywordsForPrompt }))) } ] }) }}

={{ JSON.stringify({ model: $json.anthropicModel, max_tokens: 3000, system: 'You are an SEO information architect. You are given a list of raw pillar-topic labels that were generated independently in separate batches, so some are near-duplicates or overly narrow variants of the same underlying pillar. Merge them into the smallest clear, non-overlapping set of top-level pillar topics that meaningfully covers all of them. Respond ONLY with valid JSON, no prose, matching exactly this shape: {\"canonicalPillars\": [{\"pillarName\": string, \"mergedFromLabels\": [string]}]}. Every raw label given must appear in exactly one mergedFromLabels array.', messages: [ { role: 'user', content: JSON.stringify(($json.distinctPillars || []).map(p => ({ rawLabel: p.rawLabel, clusterCount: p.clusterCount, sampleClusterTopics: p.sampleClusterTopics }))) } ] }) }}

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ model: $json.anthropicModel, max_tokens: 1500, system: 'You are a senior SEO information architect reviewing a proposed pillar/cluster/supporting-page site architecture generated from a large keyword list. Given each pillar\'s name, how many clusters and total keywords it has, assess whether the architecture is well-balanced, flag any pillars that look too thin (few clusters/keywords - should probably be merged into a related pillar or deprioritized) or too broad (should probably be split into two pillars), recommend an internal-linking pattern for a hub-and-spoke structure, and suggest a priority order for building the pillars out first. Respond ONLY with valid JSON, no prose, matching exactly this shape: {\"architectureAssessment\": string, \"thinPillars\": [string], \"broadPillars\": [string], \"internalLinkingRecommendation\": string, \"suggestedPillarPriority\": [string]}.', messages: [ { role: 'user', content: 'Total keywords: ' + $json.architectureSummary.totalKeywordsIngested + '\nPillars: ' + JSON.stringify(($json.pillars || []).map(p => ({ pillarName: p.pillarName, clusterCount: p.clusterCount, totalKeywords: p.totalKeywords }))) } ] }) }}
